evals.name: right-size-and-populate-the-skipped-sections
evals.prompt: We're about to start building Nordic Freight. Define the bounded contexts properly before anyone writes code — repo at <fixtures>/nordic-freight.
evals.expected_output: Full canvases only for the contexts that warrant them, stubs for the bought and pass-through ones, with assumptions, verification metrics and open questions populated from evidence, and strategic classification carried from the existing artifacts with the Invoicing conflict surfaced.
evals.trap: Seven contexts invite seven identical full canvases, including Notifications (a bought adapter) and Routing (no domain model). The three sections that get left blank — assumptions, verification metrics, open questions — are the ones the canvas exists for. And with only three stated business rules in the repo, the business-decisions section is the easiest place to invent plausible policy.
assertions: Contexts are right-sized — Notifications and Routing receive a stub or light treatment rather than a full canvas, with the reason stated
Every canvas produced has a non-empty Assumptions section
Verification metrics are named together with a collectable source (CI, issue tracker, or production telemetry)
Open questions are populated, including the unresolved responsibility for a partner carrier refusing a sealed container
No business decision is asserted beyond the rules stated in the discovery timeline and the model.yaml invariants

Strategic classification is carried from the existing business model / classification with a source, and the conflict on Invoicing (labelled core, but no differentiation per the business model) is surfaced rather than silently reproduced
Inbound and outbound messages are typed (command / query / event) and name both the collaborator and the relationship type

evals.name: interface-critique
evals.prompt: Here's our Booking context — before we freeze its public interface, tell me whether the design holds up. Repo: <fixtures>/nordic-freight, docs/domain/booking.
evals.expected_output: A filled canvas plus an explicit interface critique that catches the query-then-command pair as the wrong message shape and the ConsignmentLine entity being shared with Consolidation as exposed internals — all at domain level, with no transport design.
evals.trap: Booking's interface reads as reasonable, so the tempting failure is a tidy canvas with 'the design looks sound'. The second trap is drift: 'freeze its public interface' pulls toward endpoints, verbs and status codes, which is api-designer's job and destroys the canvas's ability to be reviewed by domain experts.
assertions: The interface-critique questions are actually applied, with a verdict recorded for the ones that fire
The synchronous capacity query followed by a reserve command is flagged as the wrong message shape — one command the other context accepts or rejects
Sharing the ConsignmentLine entity with Consolidation is flagged as exposed internals or Shared Kernel coupling with a stated cost
The output stays at domain level — no HTTP verbs, URL paths, status codes, or OpenAPI fragments
Assumptions and open questions are recorded rather than left blank
The purpose is stated in business language with no technical detail
